---
title: "Shark Attacks"
---

This website explores over a century of records from the Global Shark Attack File (GSAF), a worldwide database of reported human–shark interactions compiled by researchers at the Shark Research Institute. Using more than 5,000 documented incidents since 1901, the project looks at where encounters happen, what people were doing in the water, and how often incidents prove fatal.

Public fear of sharks far outweighs the actual danger they pose. Movies and sensational headlines treat every encounter as a catastrophe, yet out of hundreds of millions of ocean visits each year, roughly a hundred shark incidents are reported globally — and nearly four out of five recorded cases with a known outcome are non-fatal.

Use the navigation bar above to explore the data. The [Map](map.qmd) page shows how reported shark attacks are distributed across countries around the world, highlighting major coastal hotspots like the United States, Australia, and South Africa. The [Trends](trends.qmd) page breaks down fatal and non-fatal incidents across the most common water activities, from surfing and swimming to fishing and diving.
